summary.text:
We need answer only valid JSON with required keys. Need produce concise architecture plan <=2000 words. Need think deeply to ensure consistency with specs, scan execution order explicit 4 stages, state machine states/transitions, timer plan (no timers likely none), priorities, initial_values, formal_assertions optional list over declared port names. Need perhaps include internal vars? Formal assertions over VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. Need maybe only output formulas matching required LTL? They say optional list of {"id","formula"} temporal/invariant assertions over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. Could include P1-P9? But qLeadA/completedServed internal not port names, so if strictly over port names only, can't use qLeadA. But optional. Need produce complete JSON. Need ensure architecture plan concise. Need include state_machine list transitions. Need timer_plan: no timers; PT durations none; reset conditions N/A. But they require timers required, PT durations, reset conditions. Could be [].

Need decide representation. Must return complete JSON. Need no markdown outside.

Need understand state machine semantics exactly. Inputs Demand FaultA FaultB. Outputs PumpA PumpB LeadA. State variables internal: LeadA, previous_demand, served (episode_served). Initial LeadA true previous_demand false served false PumpA/B false. Each scan sample inputs once, read retained pre-state q[k], execute one transition, observe outputs at end same scan. Updated state q[k+1]. Need explicit scan order 4-stage:
1 edge sampling
2 safety/reset priority & state transitions
3 unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF
4 unified output assignments.
No timers, so step 3 no-op. Stage1 sample Demand, FaultA, FaultB and compute falling_edge := previous_demand AND NOT Demand? Or edge sampling; previous_demand tracking at stage? Need describe. "previous_demand tracks I[k].Demand on every scan." Since outputs same scan based on current Demand and prior state. At stage2 transition uses sampled inputs and previous_demand from previous scan. At end update previous_demand := Demand? Or stage1 record edge with old previous_demand then update at end? Need specify in scan order. Need "edge sampling": capture current inputs to scan variables, compute falling_edge := previous_demand AND NOT Demand (served gating). Then stage2 compute state. Stage4 outputs. After/within stage2 update previous_demand? Need avoid stale. Let's define stage1: sample Demand, FaultA, FaultB into scan-latched variables; compute fallingEdge := previous_demand AND NOT Demand (using prior scan's previous_demand). Stage2: evaluate transitions and update state variables including previous_demand := sampled Demand after using fallingEdge. That's okay. Need output LeadA reflects post-transition preference.

State machine could be high-level modes:
- IDLE_NO_DEMAND (Demand false): outputs both off. On falling edge with served true toggle LeadA; clear served. Update previous_demand false. Stay idle.
- DEMAND_SERVING (Demand true): determine outputs: if healthy lead exists, run it; else if other healthy, run standby; else none. If any run, served true (latch). LeadA unchanged. Stay demand. On demand false transition to IDLE_NO_DEMAND with toggle if served true. But state machine can use states with condition. Alternatively states: IDLE, DEMAND_RUN_LEAD, DEMAND_RUN_STANDBY, DEMAND_BOTH_FAULT, OFF_EPISODE_END? Need concise. They ask list states and transitions. Need maybe state machine with states IDLE, DEMAND, and transitions. But "list of states and transitions" can be detailed. Need avoid exhaustive traces. Need include internal state updates.

Need consider P6/P7: Toggle exactly when completedServed = prev demand AND !Demand AND served. completedServed uses reference state? "Spre.reference.state.demand AND NOT I[k].Demand AND Spre.reference.state.served" Hmm qLeadA previous observed output. P6: G(completedServed -> (LeadA <-> !qLeadA)). P7: G(!completedServed -> (LeadA <-> qLeadA)). This means LeadA toggles only on falling edge after served, else unchanged. Need implement. Note if Demand false and previous_demand true and served true, toggle at that scan. served reset false. If Demand stays false, no further toggle because previous_demand false or served false.

Need outputs: When Demand false both off. When Demand true:
- if LeadA true: if !FaultA then PumpA true PumpB false; else if !FaultB then PumpB true PumpA false; else both false. Wait P4 says Demand & LeadA & !FaultA -> PumpA. P5 Demand & !LeadA & !FaultB -> PumpB. P8 Demand & FaultA & !FaultB -> PumpB. P9 Demand & FaultB & !FaultA -> PumpA. If LeadA true and FaultA true and FaultB false -> fallback B. If LeadA false and FaultB true and FaultA false -> fallback A. If both healthy, lead runs only. If both fault, neither. If LeadA true and FaultA false, A. If LeadA false and FaultB false, B. At most one pump: if LeadA true FaultA true FaultB false B; if LeadA false FaultB true FaultA false A. Good.
- if either pump runs that scan (Demand true and healthy at least one), served := true. If both fault/no run, served stays previous? Requirement "If either pump runs on this scan, mark served := TRUE." What if no pump runs? Should served remain as previous? It's episode memory. If prior scans in same demand episode served true, and now both fault, then served should probably remain true? Requirement says "If either pump runs on this scan, mark served := TRUE"; it doesn't explicitly clear on no run. "episode memory served := FALSE" initial. "if previous_demand = TRUE AND served = TRUE, toggle ... reset served := FALSE" on Demand false. So served is latching once any pump runs in episode. If later both fault, served remains true and on falling edge will toggle (because episode actually delivered earlier). So implementation: if Demand true AND (PumpA OR PumpB) then served := TRUE; don't reset on no-run. On Demand false: if previous_demand AND served then toggle; served := false. Good.
- LeadA unchanged during demand, except post-transition on falling edge.

Need maybe state machine states:
S0_OFF_INIT / IDLE (Demand false)
S1_DEMAND_ACTIVE (Demand true)
Could include substate? For transition actions:
IDLE: 
  if Demand true -> DEMAND_ACTIVE, no Lead toggle, served remains? Wait if Demand false then becomes true, served should be false from idle. If Demand true transition to active, calculate output run. Should served set if pump runs. Lead unchanged. previous_demand true.
  if Demand false -> remain IDLE; if previous_demand & served then toggle Lead; served := false; outputs off; previous_demand false.
But on first scan Demand true from initial previous_demand false served false -> active; outputs based on LeadA true; if healthy mark served true.
DEMAND_ACTIVE:
  if Demand true -> remain, compute pump outputs and mark served if any; Lead unchanged; previous_demand true.
  if Demand false -> IDLE, if served true toggle Lead; served false; outputs off; previous_demand false.
This is enough. But outputs in DEMAND_ACTIVE can have subcases: run lead, fallback, both fault. Could list transitions with guards/actions. Need maybe include "S1_RunLeadA", "S1_RunLeadB", "S1_RunFallbackA", "S1_RunFallbackB", "S1_BothFault"? Hmm state machine probably expected states/transitions not just modes. But concise.

Need maybe produce JSON with state_machine as list of states objects and transitions list. Could have:
"state_machine": {
 "states": ["IDLE","DEMAND"],
 "transitions": [
  {"from":"IDLE","to":"IDLE","guard":"NOT Demand","actions":["PumpA=FALSE","PumpB=FALSE","IF previous_demand AND served THEN LeadA:=NOT LeadA END_IF","served:=FALSE","previous_demand:=FALSE"]},
  {"from":"IDLE","to":"DEMAND","guard":"Demand","actions":["served:=served (no fallingedge)","previous_demand:=TRUE"]},
  {"from":"DEMAND","to":"DEMAND","guard":"Demand","actions":["SelectPumps()","IF PumpA OR PumpB THEN served:=TRUE END_IF","previous_demand:=TRUE"]},
  {"from":"DEMAND","to":"IDLE","guard":"NOT Demand","actions":["PumpA=FALSE","PumpB=FALSE","IF served THEN LeadA:=NOT LeadA END_IF","served:=FALSE","previous_demand:=FALSE"]}
 ]
}
But transition from IDLE guard NOT Demand to IDLE actions includes toggle if previous_demand & served. But if current Demand false and state IDLE, previous_demand could be true only on falling edge scan, because if previous scan demand true then state DEMAND and now Demand false; state machine prior state DEMAND, not IDLE. Actually if state is DEMAND and guard NOT Demand, transition to IDLE toggles. After that same scan outputs off. Next scan state IDLE Demand false guard NOT Demand, previous_demand was set false, so no toggle. In IDLE->IDLE we could action reset served false and no toggle because previous_demand should false. But if state representation updated state previous_demand maybe true? Need ensure one transition. Could use transition from DEMAND to IDLE handles toggle. IDLE->IDLE can just reset served? But if served somehow true? After falling edge reset. Keep robust: IDLE self on !Demand: both off; no toggle (since previous_demand already false in IDLE); maybe served := false. Need not include toggle because transition from DEMAND handles it. But if previous_demand true and served true while state IDLE impossible under normal. However state machine should explicitly: in OFF state when Demand false, if previous_demand and served then toggle and clear; this matches req. Could define state variables and transition actions independent of state: Every scan:
if Demand false:
  if previous_demand and served toggle LeadA
  served := false
  pump off
else:
  select pumps; if any run served true
previous_demand := Demand
LeadA unchanged otherwise.
This is simpler than state machine; but they require state_machine. Use states IDLE/DEMAND with actions. Need be careful IDLE->IDLE might include toggle guard previous_demand AND served. Since previous_demand updated at end, on first IDLE scan after prior demand? Actually state before transition is DEMAND, not IDLE, because prior scan Demand true. So DEMAND->IDLE handles toggle. In IDLE state, previous_demand should be false from prior scan if coming from IDLE. But if initial previous_demand false. So fine. But if there is a reset or state started IDLE with previous_demand true? Could be not. But requirement explicitly "When Demand = FALSE: both off; if previous_demand = TRUE AND served = TRUE, toggle LeadA; reset served := FALSE." That applies regardless state. So include in IDLE self transition as well: IF previous_demand AND served THEN toggle. But then if state DEMAND->IDLE AND then same scan? No only one transition. If transition from DEMAND to IDLE includes toggle; next scan IDLE self sees previous_demand false, no toggle. Good. If state IDLE and Demand false with previous_demand true & served true due to weird, self transition toggles once. Then sets previous_demand false. Good.

Need maybe combine states as "OFF" and "DEMAND". Transitions:
- OFF (!Demand) -> OFF: PumpA/B false; if prevDemand && served toggle LeadA; served false; prevDemand false.
- OFF (Demand) -> DEMAND: evaluate pumps and mark served if any; prevDemand true; LeadA unchanged.
- DEMAND (Demand) -> DEMAND: evaluate pumps and mark served if any; prevDemand true; LeadA unchanged.
- DEMAND (!Demand) -> OFF: PumpA/B false; if served toggle LeadA; served false; prevDemand false.
This covers. For OFF(!Demand) toggle condition uses prevDemand && served; but in OFF state prevDemand may be true only first scan after demand? Wait state after previous scan was DEMAND, not OFF, because Demand true. So transition from DEMAND(!Demand)->OFF occurs same scan. Therefore OFF self does not need toggle but include for correctness if state set differently. Fine.

Need "edge sampling" compute fallingEdge: previous_demand AND NOT Demand. Could use guard "fallingEdge && served" for toggle. In transition actions use fallingEdge & served. But if OFF self guard !Demand and fallingEdge maybe true if state OFF? State OFF with prevDemand true could happen initial? Not normally. Fine.

Need timer_plan: [] or object. They ask "timer_plan: timers required, PT durations, reset conditions". Could be:
"timer_plan": {
  "timers": [],
  "PT_durations": "none",
  "reset_conditions": "N/A; implementation is scan-count independent and has no timed delays"
}
or list. They said keys maybe timer_plan: list? Not specified shape. Use object with "timers":[], "PT_durations":{}, "reset_conditions":"N/A". Need JSON valid. Could use array for timers. Maybe better:
"timer_plan": {
 "required": false,
 "timers": [],
 "pt_durations": {},
 "reset_conditions": "No timers used; served/previous_demand reset as described on demand falling edge/scan update."
}
Need maybe "reset_conditions" for internal? But timer plan no timers. Fine.

Need "priorities": safety and operational priorities. List:
1 Faulted pumps never energized.
2 No demand forces both off.
3 At most one pump runs.
4 Demand true: healthy selected lead first; if lead faulted, healthy standby fallback; if both fault, neither.
5 Alternate lead only on falling edge after served episode.
6 Track previous_demand every scan, latch served if any pump runs during episode.
Need include.

Need "initial_values": include input? Outputs? Internal. Spec initial values. Use:
{
 "Demand": false? Inputs maybe not initialized? They didn't specify inputs initial; but initial conditions include LeadA true previous_demand false episode_served false PumpA false PumpB false. Could include "inputs": {"Demand": false, "FaultA": false, "FaultB": false}? But initial_conditions doesn't specify. Better include only specified plus internal alias episode_served false. Maybe include scan vars? They ask initial values for variables. Include "LeadA": true, "previous_demand": false, "served": false, "episode_served": false, "PumpA": false, "PumpB": false, maybe "fallingEdge": false, "scanDemand": false, "scanFaultA": false, "scanFaultB": false. But avoid overdo. Need initial PumpA/B and LeadA output. Good.

Need "scan_execution_order": explicit 4-stage scan order (1 edge sampling, 2 safety/reset priority & state transitions, 3 unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF, 4 unified output assignments). Need represent as array of four objects:
1: "Sample Demand, FaultA, FaultB once into scan-latched variables. Compute fallingEdge := previous_demand AND NOT Demand. Do not write outputs here."
2: "Apply safety/reset priority and transition state: if not Demand, force pump commands off, if fallingEdge AND served then toggle LeadA; served:=FALSE; if Demand, select healthy pump per LeadA/fallback, set served if any pump runs; update previous_demand:=scanDemand. Updated state retained for next scan."
Need order in stage2: maybe safety/reset priority before state transitions. Also "No demand forces both off" first. Fault gate in selection. Should mention LeadA post-transition. Need ensure previous_demand update after using fallingEdge. 
3: "No timer FBs; unconditional timer calls would be placed here; none implemented."
4: "Unified output assignments: PumpA := ...; PumpB := ...; LeadA := lead_pref_post; write outputs once at scan end." Need maybe outputs assigned from state results: PumpA/PumpB computed, LeadA post. Need maybe no duplicate coil assignments elsewhere.
Need include "edge sampling" and stage 2 transitions. Good.

Need "formal_assertions": optional list. Since requested "optional list", but likely include. Need formulas over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. Could include P1-P5,P8,P9 exactly using port names. P6/P7 involve qLeadA internal, cannot strictly over ports only. But maybe we can include them with "qLeadA" not port, violates "over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names". They specifically ask optional list of assertions over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. So include only port-name formulas:
A1 G(!(PumpA & PumpB))
A2 G((!Demand | FaultA) -> !PumpA)
A3 G((!Demand | FaultB) -> !PumpB)
A4 G((Demand & LeadA & !FaultA) -> PumpA) (LeadA is output previous/current? In LTL over outputs at same scan. This is from spec. But note LeadA current output may be toggled on falling edge only when Demand false, so when Demand true LeadA equals preference. Good.)
A5 G((Demand & !LeadA & !FaultB) -> PumpB)
A6 G((Demand & FaultA & !FaultB) -> PumpB)
A7 G((Demand & FaultB & !FaultA) -> PumpA)
Maybe A8 G(!Demand -> !PumpA & !PumpB) safety. This is port-only. A9 G((Demand & !FaultA & !FaultB & LeadA) -> PumpA & !PumpB) maybe redundant. Keep concise.
Need be careful with formula syntax. They said temporal/invariant assertions over declared port names. Use strings with G(...). Fine. If using "->" and "&" etc. Ensure JSON escaping not needed. Use standard. Include id and formula only. Could include all P1-P5,P8,P9 plus no demand off. The spec P2/P3 already imply no demand -> !PumpA and !PumpB. P1 at most one. Could include "G(!Demand -> (!PumpA & !PumpB))" as A1. Then include P1 etc. But maybe avoid duplication. Need ensure formulas don't include internal qLeadA. Good.
Could include assertion for toggling? Cannot with ports only because need previous LeadA. But LTL can express X? Could: G((Demand & !FaultA...) no. Toggle on falling edge after served cannot express served without internal. But we can express preference alternation maybe using next? Not necessary. Optional.

Need maybe state_machine include "states" and "transitions". Need no exhaustive traces. Keep under 2000 words.

Potential issue: "initial preference LeadA := TRUE" but LeadA is an output. It reflects post-transition preference. On initial scan if Demand false, LeadA remains true. Good. Stage4 output LeadA := lead_pref_post (state). On first scan, LeadA true.

Need decide if state_machine transitions should include outputs in actions? Stage4 unified output assignments, so transitions should update state variables not output coils maybe. But LeadA is both output and state; in PLC, can use variable as state and output at end. To align stage order, stage2 updates "lead_pref_post" internal, stage4 assigns LeadA := lead_pref_post. Or LeadA itself retained. Need include state variable "lead_pref" internal? Spec says LeadA reflects post-transition preference and is output. Could treat LeadA as retained state and output variable. But scan_execution_order stage2 "toggle LeadA" and stage4 "LeadA := LeadA_post"? To avoid multiple assignment, use internal "LeadA_state" or "lead_pref". But interface only LeadA. In architecture plan, we can use internal variables: LeadA_State, Served, PreviousDemand. Stage2 updates LeadA_State, stage4 assigns LeadA := LeadA_State. Initial LeadA_State true. This is clean. Need include initial_values maybe "LeadA_State": true. But spec initial LeadA true. We can mention "LeadA_State (backing state for LeadA)". Formal assertions use LeadA output. Good.

Need perhaps state_machine transitions with internal variables:
States: "S0_OFF" and "S1_DEMAND".
Transition S0_OFF --(!scanDemand)--> S0_OFF:
 actions:
  - PumpCmdA := FALSE; PumpCmdB := FALSE; (or stage4?)
  - IF fallingEdge AND Served THEN LeadA_State := NOT LeadA_State END_IF
  - Served := FALSE
  - PreviousDemand := FALSE
But fallingEdge uses previous_demand. If PreviousDemand updated at end, good. However in S0_OFF with !Demand and PreviousDemand maybe true? FallingEdge true. If state S0_OFF previous scan Demand false, previous_demand false. Fine. But if transition S1_DEMAND --(!scanDemand)--> S0_OFF: actions same. Good.
Transition S0_OFF --(scanDemand)--> S1_DEMAND:
  - LeadA_State unchanged
  - Select outputs based on LeadA_State etc.
  - IF PumpCmdA OR PumpCmdB THEN Served:=TRUE END_IF (else leave)
  - PreviousDemand := TRUE
Transition S1_DEMAND --(scanDemand)--> S1_DEMAND:
  - Select outputs
  - IF PumpCmdA OR PumpCmdB THEN Served:=TRUE END_IF
  - PreviousDemand := TRUE
Transition S1_DEMAND --(!scanDemand)--> S0_OFF:
  - PumpCmdA/B false
  - IF Served THEN LeadA_State := NOT LeadA_State END_IF (or fallingEdge AND served)
  - Served := FALSE
  - PreviousDemand := FALSE
Need include fallingEdge computed stage1. In S1_DEMAND->S0_OFF, previous_demand should be true if state DEMAND because previous scan demand true, but can use fallingEdge. Guard !Demand. Since previous_demand true, fallingEdge true. Use "IF fallingEdge AND Served". Good. But if state S1_DEMAND somehow entered with previous_demand false? Not. But use fallingEdge.

Need selection function:
SelectPumps:
IF NOT scanDemand THEN PumpCmdA:=FALSE; PumpCmdB:=FALSE
ELSIF LeadA_State AND NOT scanFaultA THEN PumpCmdA:=TRUE; PumpCmdB:=FALSE
ELSIF NOT LeadA_State AND NOT scanFaultB THEN PumpCmdA:=FALSE; PumpCmdB:=TRUE
ELSIF LeadA_State AND scanFaultA AND NOT scanFaultB THEN PumpCmdA:=FALSE; PumpCmdB:=TRUE  // fallback to B
ELSIF NOT LeadA_State AND scanFaultB AND NOT scanFaultA THEN PumpCmdA:=TRUE; PumpCmdB:=FALSE  // fallback to A
ELSE PumpCmdA:=FALSE; PumpCmdB:=FALSE
END_IF
But order could simplify:
IF LeadA_State THEN
  IF NOT FaultA THEN A := TRUE ELSE IF NOT FaultB THEN B:=TRUE ELSE both false
ELSE
  IF NOT FaultB THEN B:=TRUE ELSE IF NOT FaultA THEN A:=TRUE ELSE both false
END_IF
Need ensure P8/P9 fallback independent of lead. This selection does. For LeadA true FaultA true FaultB false => B true. For LeadA false FaultB true FaultA false => A true. Good.
Need at most one pump: branches assign one or none.

Could include in state_machine transitions "selection actions follow SelectHealthyPump()" and maybe separate "pump_selection" key? Required keys fixed, can add? They said return complete JSON with keys. We can include extra? Better not extra top-level keys beyond specified? "with keys:" means include those; extra maybe okay but avoid. We can embed selection in transitions or priorities. Need state_machine list of states and transitions maybe include selection in transitions. Could include "state_machine": {"states": [...], "transitions": [...], "selection_rules": [...]} but extra nested okay? They asked list of states and transitions. Could include "pump_selection" inside state_machine? Maybe not. Keep transitions actions with "SelectHealthyPump()" and define selection in priorities? Might be less explicit. Need architecture plan enough. We can add within state_machine a "selection_logic" field; JSON still complete. But they said state_machine: list of states and transitions. Hmm could be object; "list of states and transitions" maybe expected array? To be safe, make state_machine an object with "states" array and "transitions" array. Include "selection_logic" string within transitions? We can write action "PumpCmdA/PumpCmdB := SelectHealthyPump(scanDemand, scanFaultA, scanFaultB, LeadA_State)" and define in priorities. But for clarity, include "pump_selection" as part of state_machine? Let's design:

"state_machine": {
  "states": [
    {"name":"OFF","meaning":"Demand false; both pump commands false; served false after edge handling"},
    {"name":"DEMAND","meaning":"Demand true; run healthy preferred pump or fallback; latch served if any run"}
  ],
  "transitions": [
    {"from":"OFF","to":"OFF","guard":"NOT Demand","actions":["PumpCmdA:=FALSE","PumpCmdB:=FALSE","IF fallingEdge AND served THEN LeadA_State:=NOT LeadA_State END_IF","served:=FALSE","previous_demand:=FALSE"]},
    {"from":"OFF","to":"DEMAND","guard":"Demand","actions":["SelectHealthyPump()","IF PumpCmdA OR PumpCmdB THEN served:=TRUE END_IF","previous_demand:=TRUE"]},
    {"from":"DEMAND","to":"DEMAND","guard":"Demand","actions":["SelectHealthyPump()","IF PumpCmdA OR PumpCmdB THEN served:=TRUE END_IF","previous_demand:=TRUE"]},
    {"from":"DEMAND","to":"OFF","guard":"NOT Demand","actions":["PumpCmdA:=FALSE","PumpCmdB:=FALSE","IF fallingEdge AND served THEN LeadA_State:=NOT LeadA_State END_IF","served:=FALSE","previous_demand:=FALSE"]}
  ],
  "SelectHealthyPump": "IF LeadA_State THEN IF NOT FaultA THEN PumpCmdA:=TRUE; PumpCmdB:=FALSE ELSIF NOT FaultB THEN PumpCmdA:=FALSE; PumpCmdB:=TRUE ELSE PumpCmdA:=FALSE; PumpCmdB:=FALSE END_IF ELSE IF NOT FaultB THEN PumpCmdA:=FALSE; PumpCmdB:=TRUE ELSIF NOT FaultA THEN PumpCmdA:=TRUE; PumpCmdB:=FALSE ELSE PumpCmdA:=FALSE; PumpCmdB:=FALSE END_IF END_IF"
}
Need note this string uses "FaultA" but should use scanFaultA. Use "scanFaultA" etc. Good. In transition guard use "scanDemand" or "Demand"? Since stage1 samples into scan variables. Use "Demand" maybe okay. But to be precise, use "scanDemand" in state transitions? Formal output uses port. In plan, use "scanDemand" as latched. But maybe evaluator expects names. Could use "Demand (sampled)" in strings. Fine.

Need "timer_plan": no timers. Could include "reset_conditions": "No timer reset. Non-timer state resets: served:=FALSE on any !Demand transition; previous_demand:=sampled Demand each scan; LeadA_State toggles only on falling edge with served." But timer plan reset conditions maybe just no timers. Keep.

Need "formal_assertions" formulas. Need ensure they are valid LTL over declared ports. Use "G(...)" with "!" "&" "|" "->" "<->". The problem's spec uses "G(!(PumpA & PumpB))". Good.
Let's choose:
[
{"id":"A1","formula":"G(!(PumpA & PumpB))"},
{"id":"A2","formula":"G(!Demand -> (!PumpA & !PumpB))"},
{"id":"A3","formula":"G((!Demand | FaultA) -> !PumpA)"},
{"id":"A4","formula":"G((!Demand | FaultB) -> !PumpB)"},
{"id":"A5","formula":"G((Demand & LeadA & !FaultA) -> PumpA)"},
{"id":"A6","formula":"G((Demand & !LeadA & !FaultB) -> PumpB)"},
{"id":"A7","formula":"G((Demand & FaultA & !FaultB) -> PumpB)"},
{"id":"A8","formula":"G((Demand & FaultB & !FaultA) -> PumpA)"}
]
Need maybe A3/A4 include no demand off. A2 redundant. Fine. Do we need assert both fault -> no pumps? "G((Demand & FaultA & FaultB) -> (!PumpA & !PumpB))". Add A9. Good.
Could also assert "G((Demand & !FaultA & !FaultB) -> (PumpA <-> LeadA) & (PumpB <-> !LeadA))" but if LeadA true, P5? Actually if both healthy, lead runs. This is port-only and correct? LeadA output current. If Demand true, LeadA not toggled, so yes. Could add but maybe enough. Keep list concise.

Need ensure no formula uses internal. Good.

Need "initial_values": maybe include:
{
 "LeadA": true,
 "LeadA_State": true,
 "previous_demand": false,
 "served": false,
 "episode_served": false,
 "PumpA": false,

}
Could include inputs? Maybe not. But initial inputs can be forbidden? The spec only initial conditions. If include "Demand": false might imply initial input but not specified. Avoid. Need mention "LeadA_State backs LeadA output" maybe not possible in JSON value. Could add "LeadA_State": true. Good.

Need "priorities" maybe array of objects? Use list strings. Keep concise.

Need "state_machine" transitions. Need ensure "OFF->OFF guard NOT Demand" actions include toggle if fallingEdge AND served. But in OFF state, previous_demand maybe false. Fine. However if Demand false and previous_demand true AND served true, state before scan would be DEMAND if previous scan Demand true. So OFF->OFF action won't execute; DEMAND->OFF will. But including toggle in both could theoretically double toggle? No because only one transition executes. But if state variable erroneously OFF with prevDemand true served true, toggles. Good.

Potential subtlety: In transition OFF->DEMAND, should served maybe reset? If previous Demand false, served should already false due to OFF->OFF. If starting initial served false. If somehow served true and Demand becomes true without falling edge (e.g., initial served true?), requirement only reset on Demand false, not on rising. But should not. Could leave served. Maybe in OFF state, on every !Demand, served false. If Demand true from OFF, served should be false from previous scan unless initial. Good.
Transition DEMAND->DEMAND when both fault: served not set (leave previous). If served was false, remains false. If served true from earlier, remains true. Good.
Transition DEMAND->OFF: toggle if fallingEdge AND served. Since guard !Demand, fallingEdge = previous_demand AND !Demand. previous_demand should true. Good. Reset served false. previous_demand false. LeadA_State toggled as post-transition. Output LeadA at same scan will be toggled (because stage4 assigns LeadA_State). Good.

Need maybe stage2 "safety/reset priority & state transitions": If !Demand, force both off regardless state; then toggle/reset; if Demand, select with fault priority. Good.

Need "scan_execution_order" exactly four stages. Could be list of four strings or objects. Use list of strings with numbers in text. They specified explicit 4-stage scan order. Maybe object with keys "1_edge_sampling", etc. But they want list? "scan_execution_order: explicit 4-stage scan order (1. edge sampling, 2. safety/reset priority & state transitions, 3. unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF, 4. unified output assignments)". Use array of four objects:
[
 {"stage":1,"name":"edge sampling","actions":"..."},
 ...
]
Need include stage 3 no timers. Good.
